summary: Sustained elevated 5xx plateau during high small-payload async fan-out causing gateway queueing
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-14 13:05 UTC we observed a persistent elevation in 5xx responses for one dedicated tenant (AcmeRetail). Error rate plateaued at ~8-12% for ~90 minutes rather than short spike. Impact: customer reports degraded product availability for async webhook inference jobs; user-facing latencies increased and several background tasks failed, causing partial data loss for ingestion pipeline. Environment: production, us-east region, Dedicated cluster for AcmeRetail. Observed behaviour: - Small payload (<= 300 tokens) async requests that fan out to 8 parallel subtasks per request triggered a sustained queue in API gateway. - Many upstream runtime workers received prefetch/cancellation signals and immediately opened new connections; observed connection churn and ephemeral worker spin-up. - API gateway responded with a mix of 502 and 504 and some 503 when proxy pools hit soft limits. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady stream of small payload async requests with fanout=8 at 350 requests/s to tenant AcmeRetail. 2) Observe gateway accept queue growth and increased 5xx. 3) Watch serving-runtime logs for frequent prefetch cancel + reconnect sequences. Key logs/metrics: - apigw.accept_queue_length peaked at ~460 (normal <50). - apigw.proxy_pool_reuse_failures spiked concurrently. - runtime.worker_launch_rate doubled and worker_uptime_short_sessions increased. - KV-prefetch lock contention observed on kvcache_shard_24. Temporary mitigation applied: - Throttled tenant to 150 rps at apigw layer and enabled short-circuit fallback to shared variant model. - Manually increased proxy pool soft limit for AcmeRetail route to reduce immediate 502s. - Notified customer of partial ingestion failure and provided retry guidance. Next steps: - Deep dive into prefetch cancellation logic and edge-case where small-payload fanout leads to accept-queue amplification. - Evaluate prioritizer fairness for small, high-fanout jobs. - Consider adding backpressure earlier in the prefetch path and making proxy pool limits adaptive.
comments: 2026-03-14 13:20 UTC - Support (Avery): Initial triage done; high 5xx observed for AcmeRetail tenant. Escalating to SRE and Runtime oncall.

2026-03-14 13:38 UTC - SRE (Jordan): Confirmed accept_queue growth and proxy pool saturation. Applied temporary tenant throttle to 150 rps and increased soft pool limit. 5xx rate decreased to ~4% after throttle.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Small-payload fanout causes the API gateway to hold many half-open upstream connections while waiting for prefetch responses; when prefetches cancel they trigger rapid reconnections rather than graceful reuse.
Hypothesis B: KV-prefetch shard locking and eviction policy leads to hot shard contention for this tenant's pattern, increasing serving-runtime CPU and delaying responses causing gateway timeouts.
Reproduction: Staging replay with 200 rps fanout=8 reproduced accept queue growth within 4 minutes; lower fanout or batching restores baseline.
Evidence: kvcache.stats shows shard_24 lock wait percent jump from 2% -> 38% concurrent with prefetch cancels. apigw proxy reuse failures rise with short-lived sessions.
Temporary workarounds evaluated: per-tenant fanout cap (reduces 5xx), tenant-level request pacing at edge (effective), prefetch cancellation debounce (partial improvement).
resolution: Workaround: Applied tenant throttle and increased proxy pool soft limit; instructed customer to retry failed jobs with idempotency keys to avoid duplicates.
Planned fix: Runtime team to land PR for safe prefetch cancellation cleanup and add socket-reuse instrumentation (target: 2026-03-20).
Operational follow-up: Console flag to cap fanout per tenant being scoped by Product Ops; SRE to autotune proxy pool thresholds based on small-payload fanout metrics.
Follow-up ticket: INT-215432 created to track infra changes for adaptive proxy pool sizing and prioritized for next maintenance window.
Customer communication: Sent interim incident summary and mitigation steps; will schedule postmortem and share with AcmeRetail by 2026-03-18.
